content: Oseltamivir is a medication prescribed to treat certain types of influenza (commonly known as the flu) in adults and children over the age of one who have experienced flu symptoms for no more than two days. It is also used to prevent certain types of flu in individuals who have been in close contact with someone infected with the flu or during a flu outbreak. Oseltamivir belongs to a class of drugs called neuraminidase inhibitors, which work by inhibiting the spread of the influenza virus within the body. This medication can help reduce the duration of flu symptoms, such as nasal congestion or discharge, sore throat, cough, muscle or joint pain, fatigue, headache, fever, and chills. However, it does not prevent bacterial infections that may arise as complications of the flu. Oseltamivir is available in capsule form and as an oral suspension (liquid). When used to treat flu symptoms, it is typically taken twice daily (morning and evening) for five days. For flu prevention, it is usually taken once daily for at least ten days or up to six weeks during a community flu outbreak. It can be taken with or without food, but taking it with food or milk may reduce the likelihood of stomach upset. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take oseltamivir exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. To prepare doses of oseltamivir liquid: Shake the bottle well for about five seconds before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Open the bottle by pressing down on the cap while turning it. Push the plunger of the provided measuring device completely down to the tip. Insert the tip of the measuring device firmly into the bottle's opening. Turn the bottle upside down with the measuring device attached. Slowly pull back on the plunger until the prescribed amount of liquid fills the device to the appropriate marking. For larger doses, you may need to measure the liquid twice. If you are unsure how to measure the dose correctly, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Turn the bottle right side up and carefully remove the measuring device. Administer the medication directly into your mouth from the measuring device without mixing it with other liquids. Replace the cap on the bottle and close it tightly. Disassemble the measuring device, rinse its parts under running tap water, and allow them to air dry before reassembling for the next use. Continue taking oseltamivir for the full duration of your prescription, even if you start feeling better. Do not stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor, as stopping too soon or skipping doses may result in incomplete treatment or inadequate flu prevention. If your symptoms worsen, new symptoms develop, or your flu symptoms do not improve, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, ask your pharmacist or doctor for a copy of the manufacturer's patient information for further guidance. Oseltamivir may also be used to treat and prevent infections caused by avian influenza (bird flu), a virus that primarily infects birds but can cause severe illness in humans. Before taking oseltamivir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to oseltamivir or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. This includes medications that affect the immune system, such as azathioprine, cyclosporine, cancer chemotherapy drugs, methotrexate, sirolimus, oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, methylprednisolone, prednisone), or tacrolimus. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have previously taken oseltamivir to treat or prevent the flu. Additionally, disclose any medical conditions that affect your immune system, such as HIV or AIDS, or if you have heart, liver, lung, or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking oseltamivir, contact your doctor immediately. Be aware that some individuals who have taken oseltamivir to treat the flu have experienced confusion, abnormal behavior, or self-harm. These symptoms were more common in children but have also been reported in adults. If your child is taking oseltamivir, monitor their behavior closely and contact the doctor immediately if they become confused or behave abnormally. If you are taking oseltamivir, ensure that your family or caregiver is aware of potential serious symptoms and can seek medical attention on your behalf if necessary. Ask your doctor whether you should receive an annual flu vaccination. Oseltamivir does not replace the need for a yearly flu vaccine. If you have received or plan to receive the intranasal flu vaccine (FluMist), inform your doctor before taking oseltamivir, as it may interfere with the vaccine's effectiveness if taken within two weeks after or 48 hours before the vaccine is administered. If you forget to take a dose of oseltamivir, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is within two hours of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. If you miss several doses, contact your doctor for further instructions. Oseltamivir may cause side effects. Mild side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache, difficulty sleeping, cough, and dizziness. Notify your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects, such as rash, hives, skin blisters, itching, swelling of the face or tongue, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or hoarseness, require immediate medical attention. Store oseltamivir capsules at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Keep the liquid form refrigerated but do not freeze it. Discard any unused liquid medication after ten days. Properly dispose of expired or unneeded medication by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include nausea and vomiting. Oseltamivir will not prevent you from transmitting the flu to others. Practice good hygiene, such as frequent handwashing and avoiding sharing cups or utensils, to reduce the spread of the virus. Do not share your medication with others, and note that your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have flu symptoms after completing the medication, contact your doctor.
